title: Decision-focused Sparse Tangent Portfolio Optimization
claim: A prediction flows through optimize, transform, soft-select and re-optimize stages, and gradients flow back through every stage end-to-end.
layout: 3 blocks, left-to-right, with pink backward-pass gradient arrows below
description: A wide horizontal diagram split into three color-coded blocks. On the left, a green box labeled Predictive Model f_theta shows a small MLP and the dataset D. In the middle, a large blue box labeled Differentiable Optimization Layer holds three rounded sub-boxes: an Optimization problem (max y^T mu-hat with constraints), a Transformation and Soft Top-K Selection stack, and a second Optimization problem. On the right, an orange box labeled Task Loss holds L_Task. Black arrows carry mu-hat, w*(0), mu-hat' and w* between blocks. Pink curved backward arrows below the blocks are labeled with partial-derivative expressions, and a pink-bordered box marks the central Jacobian. A legend at top right distinguishes forward from backward passes.
caption: Overview of the proposed differentiable decision layer. Given predicted returns ˆµ, the layer performs optimize →score transform →soft top-k selection →re-optimize to produce sparse tangent portfolio weights, which define the task loss. Backpropagation flows through all steps, enabling end-to-end DFL. A central technical challenge is differentiating the optimization-based decision layer with respect to the prediction ˆµ.
abstract: Sparse tangent portfolio optimization aims to learn an interpretable, low-cardinality portfolio in the tangency direction of the mean-variance frontier. However, the associated cardinality-constrained formulation is NP-hard, and standard predict-then-optimize pipelines often misalign forecasting accuracy with downstream portfolio quality. We propose an end-to-end decision-focused learning framework that reformulates Sharpe ratio maximization as a Disciplined Parametrized Programming (DPP)-compliant convex programming layer and replaces discrete selection with a smooth top-$k$ operator enforcing an exact cardinality $k$. This enables gradient flow through prediction, asset selection, and re-optimization, allowing the predictive model to directly optimize portfolio performance. Across four major equity markets, our method achieves competitive and often superior out-of-sample Sharpe ratios compared with historical and prediction-focused baselines, with particularly strong gains in larger asset universes. Our \href{https://github.com/feuerwerksh/Diffble-card-SR}{code} is publicly available.
